papers.title_en: An entangling Hubbard quasiparticle collider on a digital quantum processor
papers.abstract_en: Scattering of quasiparticles provides direct access to the interactions that govern strongly correlated systems. In this work, we realize the quasiparticle scattering experiment of the Fermi-Hubbard model on a digital quantum processor by colliding a doublon and a holon in the half-filled chain of 21 sites encoded on 42 qubits of the ibm_boston processor. For the first time, we measure the transmission probability of quasiparticles of the Hubbard model on quantum hardware, which agrees with the Bethe-ansatz scattering matrix without free parameters. Beyond the scattering probabilities, the collision generates entanglement by superposing the transmitted and reflected components, which we infer from the particle-number fluctuation. In sharp contrast, a control collision between two doublons shows neither the interaction dependence nor the number fluctuation, as expected for indistinguishable particles. Our work demonstrates that the ability to create quasiparticles of a chosen flavor on demand and program their motion and interactions makes a digital quantum processor a new experimental toolset for probing the entanglement structure generated by quasiparticle scattering.

papers.title_en: A possible detection of gas rotation in galaxy groups via the kinetic Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect
papers.abstract_en: We utilise the kinetic Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect (kSZ) to measure the rotation of ionised gas within galaxy groups defined in the SDSS-DR7 galaxy sample, via their dipolar imprint on the cosmic microwave background (CMB). We estimate the direction of the projected angular momentum for each of our selected fast-rotating groups by measuring the redshift dipole of satellite galaxies around their group centres. We find a clear redshift dipole in the stacked data for the selected SDSS groups. We then perform oriented stacking of the Planck CMB temperature map using the group centres and directions of angular momenta. We report a $2.3σ$ tentative detection of the dipolar rotational kSZ effect (rkSZ) within the virial radii of our fast-rotating groups from SDSS with an average mass of $10^{14}h^{-1} \rm M_{\odot}$ (corresponding to a null-hypothesis probability of 0.96%). We estimate the averaged rotational velocity of the sample to be $\sim 100-200 ~\rm km ~s^{-1}$, reaching a maximum value of $158.8\pm13.6 ~\rm km ~s^{-1}$. Our results are consistent within the errors with predictions based on the ELUCID constrained realisation simulation, with the predicted amplitude of the rkSZ signal being slightly lower near the centre. We also identify a systematic bias when estimating rotational velocities using the observed redshifts of galaxies, but find it to be subdominant for our analysis.

papers.title_en: A universal sector of $\mathcal{N}=1$ class $\mathcal{S}$ spectra
papers.abstract_en: We determine a universal sector of the spectrum of light operators in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ class $\mathcal{S}$ superconformal field theories arising from M5-branes wrapped on a compact hyperbolic Riemann surface $Σ_2$. We work at large $N$, analysing Kaluza--Klein fluctuations about the dual Bah--Beem--Bobev--Wecht anti-de Sitter backgrounds for general values of the twist parameter $z$. To obtain these spectra, we specialise recently derived mass operators to modes that are constant on $Σ_2$ by imposing a suitable $z$-dependent generalised $G$-structure. We then organise the resulting eigenstates into long and protected $\mathcal{N}=1$ supermultiplets with definite flavour quantum numbers. As $z$ varies, rich patterns emerge in the spectrum, including both isolated multiplets and infinite towers of multiplets, which we characterise analytically.

papers.title_en: The LZ inelastic splitting as a probe of anomaly mediation
papers.abstract_en: The LZ 248 keV recoil candidate admits an interpretation in terms of pseudo-Dirac dark matter with a mixing-suppressed inelastic $Z$ interaction. In the MSSM, the Higgsino limit conflicts with the adopted solar-neutrino bound, while a gaugino realization requires an unprotected mass degeneracy. We realize such spectra in the MRSSM, where an $R$-symmetric Dirac bino produces the required $Z$ transition and wino coannihilation supplies the observed relic abundance. We impose the Higgs and gauge coupling relations of $N=2$ supersymmetry at a high scale and evolve them to low energy. With the remaining model parameters held fixed, we obtain spectra spanning roughly 300-850 GeV that satisfy the adopted constraints and have a small diagonal axial current. If anomaly mediation dominates the Majorana splitting, its local scale is tens of MeV for splittings of a few hundred keV. A five-dimensional warped construction generates this scale through Goldberger-Wise stabilization and a loop correction to the no-scale Kähler potential. The spectra remain testable through elastic scattering, solar neutrinos and long-lived charged states.

papers.title_en: Adiabatic evolution of hadronic neutron stars
papers.abstract_en: In this paper we compute several structural properties of static and rotating neutron stars, considering both rigid and differential rotation. To this end, we use a finite-temperature beta-stable equation of state (EOS) extending the zero-temperature hadronic EOS derived by Fortin et al. (2017). We account for the formation of hyperons and the presence of a neutrino-trapped component. Our goal is to provide insights into the long-term evolution of a protoneutron star (PNS) formed after a core-collapse supernova (CCSN) or a remnant resulting from a binary neutron star merger (BNSM). The EOS is derived using a relativistic mean-field quantum many-body theory within the Hartree approximation. Coupling constants are determined using experimental data on hypernuclei and hypernuclear matter to better account for uncertainties in hyperon single-particle potentials. Our EOS models reproduce the typical features of cold neutron stars and PNSs for nucleonic and hyperonic compositions. In particular, they are consistent with measured masses (2.01 M_sun and 2.14 M_sun for PSR J0348+0432 and PSR J0740+6620) and dimensionless tidal deformabilities from GW170817. Thermal contributions act differently depending on composition and rotation state. Finally, our evolutionary scheme provides a simple way to interpret the long-term evolution of BNSM remnants or PNSs from CCSNe, complementing dynamical simulations unable to cover full evolutionary timescales.

papers.title_en: A Note on the Feynman Lectures on Gravitation
papers.abstract_en: Following Feynman's lectures on gravitation, we consider the theory of the gravitational (massless spin-2) field in flat spacetime and present the third- and fourth-order Lagrangian densities for the gravitational field. In particular, we present detailed calculations for the third-order Lagrangian density. We point out that the expression for the third-order Lagrangian density which Feynman provided is not a solution of Feynman's condition that the third-order Lagrangian density must satisfy. However, Feynman's third-order Lagrangian density gives the correct perihelion shift.

papers.title_en: $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson Volumes from the Spectral Edge of DSSYK and Supersymmetric Extensions
papers.abstract_en: The $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes of Do and Norbury are the top-degree parts of Okuyama's discrete volumes, which are defined by topological recursion on the spectral curve of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We show that the same q-deformed volumes can be obtained from a double-scaled matrix model whose disk density is found by zooming in on the soft edges of the DSSYK density. Applying the same procedure to the hard edge of $\mathcal{N}=1$ DSSYK, we obtain candidate $q$-deformed $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes. They are polynomials of fixed degree, and they reduce to the $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes in a scaled $q\to1$ limit. These candidate volumes differ from the $\mathcal{N}=1$ volumes of Do and Norbury in (arXiv:2510.12431) up to what we call "irrelevant" contributions which exactly vanish in the scaled $q\to 1$ limit. Together, these results demonstrate how q-deformed volumes can be naturally associated to the spectral edges of various DSSYK models and provides an intuitive way to construct them in supersymmetric contexts.

papers.title_en: Reflected entropy and islands in JT gravity from partial dimensional reduction
papers.abstract_en: We study how mixed-state correlations reorganize across island transitions in Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity coupled to a non-gravitating bath. Using the partial-dimensional-reduction realization of double holography, we compute reflected entropy for adjacent and disjoint radiation regions in the vacuum and in the thermofield-double state of an eternal black hole. Reflected entropy probes the internal partition of the entanglement wedge and therefore resolves structure that is invisible to the ordinary Page curve: its dominant saddle can change even when the entropy saddle of the union remains fixed, and it vanishes at leading order when the entanglement wedge disconnects. We show that the lower-dimensional reflected-island description agrees, to leading order in the dynamical brane fluctuation, with the higher-dimensional defect-extremal-surface picture. The finite-angle comparison further suggests a projection-covariant identification of island and brane endpoints at linear order. The resulting Page-like curves and Markov gaps provide a geometric probe of the reorganization of the purification and of non-Markovian, multipartite correlation structure during island transitions.

papers.title_en: Unifying spherical convolutions through lifting
papers.abstract_en: We develop a unified description of convolution on the sphere by lifting to the rotation group. A number of definitions of spherical convolution have been proposed, differing in whether the kernel is axisymmetric or directional, whether the output is on the sphere or the rotation group, whether the signals carry spin, and in their computational cost. No unified treatment exists. Regarding the sphere as the homogeneous space $S^2 \cong \text{SO(3)}/\text{SO(2)}$, we lift a spin $s$ field to the rotation group, convolve on $\text{SO(3)}$, and project back to the sphere through the adjoint of the lift for a potentially different spin $s'$. We recover every rotation-equivariant convolution considered previously through constraints on the kernel, spin choices and inclusion or omission of the lift and projection. For maps between fields of fixed input and output spin, we prove that directional kernels, output on the sphere and equivariance cannot be achieved simultaneously. We make explicit that spin fields are sections of associated line bundles, linking the physics and bundle literatures, and express the spin rotation phase as the character of the twist of the section. We present harmonic-space algorithms for the exact and efficient computation of lifted spherical convolutions of band-limited fields by appealing to sampling theorems on the sphere and rotation group. All operators are implemented in the open-source s2conv code, and numerical experiments confirm the reductions and the equivariance of the operators to machine precision. Finally, we illustrate the operators on fields measured on the Earth and on the celestial sky.

papers.title_en: Quark and lepton mixing in the asymptotically safe Standard Model
papers.abstract_en: The quark mixing (CKM) matrix is near-diagonal, whereas the lepton mixing (PMNS) matrix is not. We learn that both observations can generically be explained within an ultraviolet completion of the Standard Model with gravity. This ultraviolet completion results in approximate relations between CKM matrix elements. The accuracy with which these hold translates into the length of asymptotically safe scaling regimes. Experimental data are consistent with the theoretical expectations arising from a fixed-point cascade at transplanckian scales. Similar results would hold for the PMNS matrix if neutrino Yukawa couplings were large. The ultraviolet complete theory, therefore, must -- and in fact can -- avoid such an outcome. It achieves this through a dynamical mechanism that limits the size of neutrino Yukawa couplings. Thus, large neutrino mixing is intimately tied to small Dirac neutrino masses, $\sum m_ν \lesssim O(1)\, \rm eV$, and a mass gap in the Standard Model fermion masses.

papers.title_en: Modular Properties of Generalised Gibbs Ensembles: The Deformed KdV Hierarchy
papers.abstract_en: We construct a set of conserved charges which are deformations of quantum KdV charges. They are associated with the modular transformation of a GGE with the spin-$σ$ KdV charge inserted with chemical potential $α_σ$. The charges are formal power series in the chemical potential, with coefficients given by local integrals of motion. We define local recursion relations and equivalent flow equations, prove commutativity to all orders, and establish uniqueness of the currents modulo total derivatives for a fixed generating series. We show that the eigenvalues of these deformed charges can be obtained from the thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz in two models. In the $c=1/2$ free fermion theory, the deformed charges reduce to explicit linear combinations of undeformed KdV charges, and their ground-state eigenvalues agree with the TBA expansion to all orders. In the Lee-Yang model, we find numerical agreement through cubic order in the spin-$5$ deformation for the first few charges evaluated on low-lying states.

papers.title_en: Beyond diagonal approximations: improved covariance modeling for pulsar timing array data analysis
papers.abstract_en: Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) searches for nHz gravitational-wave backgrounds (GWBs) typically model time-correlated noise by assuming a diagonal covariance in Fourier space, neglecting inter-frequency correlations introduced by the finite observation window. We show that this diagonal approximation can produce method-dependent shifts in estimates of spectral parameters, especially for pulsars with shallow intrinsic red noise spectra. To address these limitations, we present a method that (i) computes the time-domain autocorrelation on a coarse grid using a fast Fourier transform (FFT), (ii) interpolates it accurately to the unevenly sampled observation times, and (iii) incorporates it into a low-rank likelihood via the Sherman--Morrison--Woodbury identity. Using both analytic covariance comparisons and end-to-end simulations inspired by the NANOGrav 15-year dataset, we demonstrate that our method captures frequency correlations faithfully, avoids Gibbs ringing, and yields estimates closer to the injected values in the realization studied with modest computational cost. As PTA datasets increase in sensitivity and complexity, our approach offers a practical and scalable path to fully accurate covariance modeling for current and future analyses.

papers.title_en: Impact of ab initio E1 strength on neutron capture rates along the nickel isotopic chain
papers.abstract_en: Nucleosynthesis simulations of the r-process require neutron capture rates for neutron-rich nuclei, many of which lie beyond experimental reach. Predicting these rates relies on theoretical calculations of the low-energy electric dipole (E1) strength near the neutron threshold. We present the first ab initio computation of the E1 strength along the nickel isotopic chain, for $^{58}$Ni and the even-even isotopes $^{68-80}$Ni. The E1 strength is obtained with the Lorentz integral transform coupled-cluster (LIT-CC) method, extended to axially symmetric reference states to reach open-shell nuclei, using two- and three-nucleon interactions from chiral effective field theory. The approach is benchmarked against the measured photoabsorption cross section of $^{58}$Ni and the E1 strength of $^{68}$Ni. Along the chain we find low-lying E1 strength above the neutron threshold that grows with neutron number. Including it in the reaction code TALYS enhances the neutron capture rates forming $^{68-78}$Ni between 3 and 10 GK, with an effect that increases with temperature and neutron number and an uncertainty dominated by the inversion of the integral transform. For $^{80}$Ni, where strong pygmy dipole strength lies just above threshold, the enhancement sets in already around 0.5 GK. Together, these results open the way to ab initio input for neutron capture rates along isotopic chains far from stability.

papers.title_en: The Redshift-Space Galaxy Power Spectrum at Two-Loop Order
papers.abstract_en: Contemporary large-scale structure analyses center around the galaxy power spectrum, modeled with one-loop perturbation theory. This description naturally breaks down at large wavenumbers, prohibiting the extraction of cosmological information from small-scale clustering. In this work, we present a complete model for the redshift-space galaxy power spectrum up to two-loop order, derived in the framework of the Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structure. This accounts for a wide variety of effects, including fifth-order galaxy bias, redshift-space distortions, small-scale non-linearities, spatial non-locality, long-wavelength bulk flows, coordinate distortions, and stochasticity, involving a total of 49 free coefficients. Our model additionally encodes all deterministic contributions to the one-loop bispectrum and trispectrum (as well as the tree-level quadspectrum and pentaspectrum), which depend on many of the same parameters. We implement the model numerically, using the \textsc{vegas} algorithm to precompute the loop integrals; this allows the full likelihood to be evaluated in milliseconds. The approach is validated using power spectra measured from high-resolution simulations, considering both dark matter and realistic galaxy samples. The extension to two-loop order greatly increases the range of scales over which the power spectrum can be modeled, with $k_{\rm max}$ rising from $0.2h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ to $0.34h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ for a luminous red galaxy sample at $z=0.5$. Much of the additional information is absorbed by the numerous fifth-order biases and counterterms; for this reason, constraints on $σ_8$ are not significantly enhanced by the inclusion of two-loop terms. Future work will assess the full implications of the two-loop model for cosmological parameter inference, both alone and in combination with higher-order statistics.

papers.title_en: Perpendicular transport in isotropic magnetic turbulence. The role of stochastic drifts
papers.abstract_en: In cosmic ray propagation through turbulent magnetic fields, transport perpendicular to the mean field plays an important role in various astrophysical environments. Numerical simulations have shown that parallel and perpendicular diffusion coefficients exhibit different energy scalings, causing their ratio to increase with energy, but a comprehensive theoretical explanation remains elusive. Here, we investigate perpendicular diffusion using test particle simulations in synthetic isotropic turbulence spanning 6-7 orders of magnitude in wavenumber, together with a theoretical extension of nonlinear guiding center theory that incorporates stochastic drifts. Our approach combines field line random walk and random guiding center drifts to describe perpendicular transport. We find that parallel and perpendicular diffusion coefficients exhibit the same energy scaling only for $r_L \lesssim 10^{-2} L_c$, where $r_L$ is the particle Larmor radius and $L_c$ is the turbulence coherence length. At higher energies, perpendicular diffusion develops a stronger energy dependence, consistently across different turbulence levels. Our theoretical model suggests that this behavior arises from stochastic drifts induced by turbulent magnetic field components parallel to the mean field.

papers.title_en: An attempt to derive the LVS from a 10d EFT perspective
papers.abstract_en: Non-perturbative scalar potentials are a central ingredient for stabilising moduli in flux compactifications. A key target in this context is the direct 10d derivation of the LVS AdS potential, i.e., the scalar potential of the Large Volume Scenario before the uplift. The familiar result, relying on 4d supergravity machinery and large volume expansion, consists of three terms of parametric form $\exp(-2aτ_s)/{\mathcal V}$, $W_0\exp(-aτ_s)/{\mathcal V}^2$, and $W_0^2/{\mathcal V}^3$. In plain 10d EFT language, the first term is an instanton-anti-instanton effect while the second term comes from a single instanton coupled to 3-form flux. When attempting to derive the suppression by the volume ${\mathcal V}$ directly from the 10d EFT, one encounters a puzzle: One expects a flux-dilution factor $1/\sqrt{\mathcal V}$ for the second term and a factor $1/{\mathcal V}^2$ from Weyl rescaling to the 4d Einstein frame for both the first and second term. Thus, the total volume suppression for these two terms is stronger than in the aforementioned 4d EFT expectations. We discuss the underlying logic in detail, also in the gaugino condensation case, but fail to find a satisfactory explanation for the mismatch. While log-corrections to the Kähler potential may be responsible, these would have to be strong enough to affect the outcome of the LVS scheme at the ${\mathcal O}(1)$ level. What is worse, the origin of the required correction remains unclear.

papers.title_en: Regular and Floquet bases for gauge and gravity theories: a non perturbative approach
papers.abstract_en: This paper presents physical interpretations of the change of basis in Heun-type equations (Heun's and their confluences and reductions) from solutions decaying at two singular points to Floquet solutions. A crucial element in these connection relations is the phase acquired by Floquet solutions when transitioning between (ir)regular singularities. We exploit a novel `kink method' to compute the quantum momentum of the solutions as convergent series, explicitly at all orders. Consequently, by integrating the Floquet solutions term by term, the acquired phase can be explicitly derived as a series as well. Given that Heun equations and their confluences describe ${\cal N}=2$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills (SYM) theories in the Nekrasov-Shatashvili (NS) background (corresponding to the quantization of Seiberg-Witten differentials) as well as black hole perturbation theory, tests and predictions can be established in both domains. Specifically, we perform a critical verification matching the acquired phase with the dual gauge period, $A_D$. On the gravity side, our explicit and systematic results agree with standard methods used to analyse the Teukolsky or Regge-Wheeler equations. This procedure provides an effective alternative to instanton and gravity computations. Ultimately, it marks the initial steps toward establishing a dictionary between integrability and gravitational quantities.

papers.title_en: The Quasiparticle Ansatz for Relativistic Continuous Matrix Product States
papers.abstract_en: The Relativistic Continuous Matrix Product State (RCMPS) ansatz introduced in arXiv:2102.07741 is a translation-invariant variational ansatz intended to approximate the ground states of gapped one-dimensional relativistic Quantum Field Theories directly in the continuum limit and in infinite volume. In this work, we develop an ansatz, referred to as the Relativistic Quasiparticle (RQP) ansatz, for the low-lying one-particle excitations of the RCMPS vacuum, as well as for solitons interpolating between two distinct degenerate vacua. The corresponding energies of these states can be obtained as the eigenvalues of an effective Hamiltonian. The RQP ansatz generalizes constructions used in the Matrix Product State and Continuous Matrix Product State literature. We apply the RQP ansatz to the sine-Gordon model and find good agreement with results from integrability for both the soliton and breather masses. We also apply the RQP ansatz to the $φ^4$ theory, in both its $\mathbb Z_2$-preserving and $\mathbb{Z}_2$-broken phases, and determine the spectrum of particles and solitons. This enables us to determine the parameter regime for which multiple stable particles exist.

papers.title_en: KSZ Velocity Reconstruction with ACT and DESI-LS using a Tomographic QML Power Spectrum Estimator
papers.abstract_en: We perform kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (kSZ) velocity reconstruction on data from ACT DR6 and DESI-LS DR9. To estimate the cross-power between kSZ velocity reconstruction and galaxy density, we make use of a novel quadratic maximum likelihood (QML) power spectrum estimator in redshift binned spherical coordinates. We find a detection of the kSZ signal from the cross-correlation between the estimated velocity field and the large-scale galaxy field of $10 σ$. We estimate an amplitude $A=0.42 \pm 0.042$ of the kSZ signal relative to a halo model prediction, possibly indicating strong feedback in massive halos, in agreement with previous studies. We compare the result to the pseudo-$C_{\ell}$ analysis on the same dataset, finding a $\sim$20% improvement in the SNR. Our work demonstrates the feasibility of an optimal QML analysis at the required resolution, and will be a powerful tool for kSZ cosmology with upcoming high-resolution surveys.

papers.title_en: An exact rotating black hole solution in Palatini Kalb-Ramond gravity
papers.abstract_en: We construct an exact stationary axisymmetric vacuum configuration in metric affine Kalb-Ramond gravity with zero cosmological constant. Independent variation of the metric, connection, and antisymmetric field yields the complete field equations and the algebraic relation between the physical and auxiliary geometries. A Kerr auxiliary metric and a closed corotating vacuum two form of fixed positive norm determine the physical metric. The tensor kernel contains the horizon generator, and the metrics, independent connection, and vacuum field share a smooth extension across the nonextremal physical Killing horizon and the rotation axes at finite radius for unequal deformation factors. We obtain an explicit sufficient domain for a causal exterior and an asymptotically locally flat end at fixed nonpolar angles. The physical Hamiltonian yields the timelike and null equations, equatorial effective potentials, circular orbit properties, radial stability, and perihelion advance. Numerical photon evolution determines the critical curve on an orthonormal observer screen. Its size, shape, and centroid depend on $ε=ξ_2b^2/[2(1+ξ_1b^2)]$ at fixed normalized mass scale and spin, with Kerr recovered at $ε=0$. Geometric observations probe this combination and retain an exact degeneracy between the curvature couplings. A static equatorial comparison with Mercury gives a conditional sensitivity of $2.30\times10^{-11}$ for $|2ε|$ under the stated angular convention and mass setting.

papers.title_en: On the Accelerated Expansion of the Universe
papers.abstract_en: If we look from a quantum perspective, the most natural way in which the universe can be created is in entangled pairs whose time flow is oppositely related. This suggests the idea of the creation of a universe-antiuniverse pair. Assuming the validity of this hypothesis, in this paper, we show that the universe expands in an accelerated manner. The same reasoning holds for the anti-universe as well. This idea does not require any form of dark energy as used in the standard cosmological model of $Λ$CDM or in the modified theories of gravity.

papers.title_en: Stress-Testing Swampland Bounds with Class S Theories
papers.abstract_en: We test the Sharpened Distance Conjecture (SharpDC) for CFTs, as well as the Refined Distance Conjecture (RDC), in AdS$_5$ gravitational spacetimes, using the CFT dual. The former provides a lower bound on the exponential mass decay rate of the tower of states becoming light at infinite distance in the conformal manifold, while the latter bounds the bulk field range that can be traversed before the exponential behaviour of the tower kicks in. We prove the SharpDC for any large $N$ Lagrangian supersymmetric gauge theory with a finite number $M$ of gauge factors and vanishing one-loop $β$-function. We also investigate whether it universally holds in the limits of large central charge, finding that it does not: We exhibit concrete examples in Class S theories where the conjecture is violated in the $M\rightarrow\infty$ limit with $N$ fixed, where the size of the bulk internal geometry is much larger than the AdS curvature scale. We also test the RDC in the moduli space of Class S theories without punctures in the large $N$ limit, showing that it amounts to a precise upper bound on the Weil-Petersson diameter of the moduli space of Riemann surfaces of genus $g$. This bound is consistent with all the mathematical literature up to date, but so far remains unproven.

papers.title_en: Evidence of Taste-Symmetry restoration for Kähler-Dirac fermions on Euclidean Dynamical Triangulations
papers.abstract_en: We study the spectrum of two-particle bound states of Kähler-Dirac fermions coupled via gravity in Euclidean Dynamical Triangulations (EDT). We work in the quenched approximation, where the geometry is allowed to fluctuate, but there is no back-reaction from the matter on the geometry. The Kähler-Dirac action respects an exact $U(1)$ symmetry that is related to continuum chiral symmetry, and this $U(1)$ symmetry ensures that some of the bound-state masses vanish in the chiral limit of vanishing fermion bare mass. The bound-state masses that are not protected by the $U(1)$ symmetry do not vanish in the chiral limit, but the scale associated with the symmetry breaking does not appear to be a physical scale like the Planck mass or the curvature scale of the emergent de Sitter background. Rather, the mass scale associated with this non-degeneracy appears to be a positive power of the lattice spacing, decreasing as the continuum limit is approached. This suggests that Kähler-Dirac fermions in EDT can be interpreted as the gravity analog of staggered fermions in flat-space lattice field theories, with similar behavior.

papers.title_en: Scalene Yang-Baxter triples realize all nearest-neighbour Hamiltonians with global additive symmetries
papers.abstract_en: We establish that bond Hamiltonian densities, up to local difference terms whose sum vanishes under periodic boundary conditions, lying in the commutant of bond operators, $w_j\pm w_{j+1}$, is a necessary and sufficient condition for a one-dimensional nearest-neighbour Hamiltonian to conserve a uniform or staggered sum of the one-site operators $w_j$. Starting from these local commutants, we show that every such Hamiltonian and its conserved charge can be obtained from monodromy matrices constructed using regular and non-regular members of scalene Yang-Baxter triples. The results hold on periodic chains of length $L\geq3$, with even length required in the staggered case. The results do not require translation invariance, and hence the interaction on each bond can be chosen independently from the full corresponding commutant. Our representation-independent construction applies in arbitrary finite local dimension and exhausts the Hamiltonians with either prescribed additive symmetry, without requiring ordinary Yang-Baxter integrability. We illustrate the construction with spin-$\tfrac12$ and spin-1 systems and discuss its relation to the double-commutant theorem. Classifying the one-site generators $w$ and their associated bond commutants provides a route to classifying such Hamiltonians with additive conserved charges.

papers.title_en: Internal translation gauging and local gravitational energy in Weyl gauge theory
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the local gravitational source and charges obtained by introducing translations as an internal Stückelberg redundancy in Weyl gauge theory. The internal-$T(4)$-invariant dressed coframe identifies the source of the translational potential with the existing coframe variational derivative, without introducing new dynamics. We derive an excitation/source equation and balance law whose structure is independent of the constitutive parameters of the parity-even quadratic torsion family. The gravitational self-current, defined relative to a specified gravitational/matter split and boundary representative, gives a density invariant under the internal gauge factors once its frame index is contracted with the coframe; this invariance neither establishes ordinary conservation nor identifies the density with the external translation Noether current. A surface charge follows by contraction with a covariantly constant internal direction, and we separately derive the three-sector Noether superpotential of generalized reducibility, with the asymptotic conditions for conservation of its flux. At the teleparallel equivalent of general relativity (TEGR) the excitation reduces to the teleparallel superpotential and the covariant coframe--connection pair gives the Schwarzschild ADM energy; flat cosmology and transverse-traceless waves give further checks. Away from TEGR, an exact solution of New General Relativity gives a charge whose fractional difference from the Kepler mass is half the deviation of the post-Newtonian spatial-curvature parameter from unity, at the adopted normalisation; independent Hamiltonian charge matching remains open. Finally, the integrable Hamiltonian charge is invariant under covariant Lagrangian boundary terms at fixed reference normalisation and presymplectic representative.

papers.title_en: Josephson junctions, superconducting circuits, and qubit for quantum technologies
papers.abstract_en: In the realm of physics, a pivotal moment occurred six decades ago when Brian Josephson made a groundbreaking prediction, setting in motion a series of events that would eventually earn him the prestigious Nobel Prize eleven years later. This prediction centered around what is now known as the Josephson effect, a phenomenon with far-reaching implications. At the heart of this effect lies the Josephson junction (JJ), a device that has become a linchpin in various scientific applications. This chapter delves into the foundational principles of the Josephson effect and the remarkable properties of JJs. From their role in metrology to their application in radiation detectors, these junctions have ushered in a new era of electronics. Exploiting the unique features of superconductive devices, such as high speed, low dissipation, and dispersion, JJs find today practical implementation in the development of superconductive qubits and nanotechnology applications.

papers.title_en: TeV Gamma-Ray Emission in the DA 495 Region from HAWC Observations of J1952+2924, J1954+2837, and J1958+2848
papers.abstract_en: Previous observations of the DA 495 region, which contains the pulsar wind nebula (PWN) DA 495 and other very-high-energy (VHE; $>100~\textrm{GeV}$) gamma-ray emitters, showed inconsistent results across different VHE experiments, including differences in the measured flux of DA 495 and in the number of reported sources. Our new dedicated analysis using 3071 days of HAWC data resolves these discrepancies. We identify three extended sources, HAWC J1952+2924 (DA 495), HAWC J1954+2837, and HAWC J1958+2848, all with curved spectra, and find a hint of a fourth source. For DA 495, a multi-wavelength analysis, including our results, radio, X-ray, and other gamma-ray data, reveals that its extended emission is best described by leptonic interactions with an inferred magnetic field of $B\sim10~μ\textrm{G}$ and that hadronic components are not required. On the other hand, we interpret the other two sources, which have no confirmed counterparts, as TeV halos associated with nearby pulsars, PSR J1954+2836 and PSR J1958+2846, respectively. These results reinforce the interpretation of DA 495 as a leptonic-dominated PWN and add two candidates to the growing population of TeV halos.

papers.title_en: Utilizing Neural Networks for Solving Functional Renormalization Group Flow Equations
papers.abstract_en: A novel physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) based approach for solving functional renormalization group flow equations is presented. We investigate the finite temperature phase transition in $O(N)$ models without relying on the large-$N$ approximation, which was used in earlier attempts with similar methods. We argue that these previous solutions cannot easily be generalized for more complex symmetries, and hence our approach can provide new insight. Our technique relies on a series of ansätze that combines the small- and large-field approximation schemes with a neural network, leading to a highly accurate approximation over the entire field range. We compare the PINNs approach with traditional grid-based Runge-Kutta results and show that the network can successfully learn the temperature, field, and scale dependencies of the effective potential in the local potential approximation.

papers.title_en: Cellular Dynamics of Helium-rich Detonation on sub-Chandrasekhar Mass White Dwarf
papers.abstract_en: Most previous efforts for hydrodynamic studies on detonation in the context of Type Ia supernovae did not take into account the scale of the cellular structure for a criterion in initiation, propagation, quenching, and the resolution requirement of detonation, whereas it is quite common to consider cell sizes in the discussion on terrestrial detonation in chemically reactive systems. In our recent study, the terrestrial cell-based theories, which incorporates the cell-size data acquired in 2D simulations of helium detonation in the double-detonation model, were demonstrated to be a powerful diagnostics in reproducing the thresholds in the initiation and quenching provided by previous studies. In the present study, 2D simulation results of the cellular detonation in the base of white-dwarf (WD) envelope are described in detail, in terms of the dynamic wave morphology and chemical abundance structure. The cellular structure is observed at a range of upstream density and envelope composition explored in the present work. C/O contamination by the WD core material reduces the cell width rapidly, as accelerated by the α-capture reaction. It is also indicated that nickel production could be significantly delayed for the C/O-rich composition. The small cell width makes it extremely demanding to resolve the detonation structure in full-star simulations of SNe Ia; this could raise a concern on the robustness of the outcomes of some numerical simulations in terms of the success and failure of detonation. This issue may be overcome by sub-grid modeling that incorporates the cellular dynamics acquired in resolved simulations.

papers.title_en: Relaxation Dark Energy: Compositional Dynamics and the Future of Cosmic Acceleration
papers.abstract_en: If cosmic acceleration is driven by a positive cosmological constant, the universe approaches an eternally accelerating de Sitter state, whose interpretation in quantum gravity remains elusive. We develop a framework in which acceleration is instead a transient stage of dark-sector relaxation towards compositional equilibrium: matter and dark energy approach a stationary density ratio, eventually diluting like pressureless matter. Guided by linear response theory and Onsager's near-equilibrium regression hypothesis, we describe this evolution through a composition variable measuring departure from equilibrium. Extending constant fractional relaxation to the full background evolution yields the dark-energy equation of state $w=w_0a^{-n}$, where $n$ is the relaxation rate per e-fold of expansion. This history connects early dark-energy suppression, an upward phantom crossing and a density maximum to a pressureless scaling future. Using DESI DR2 BAO and Planck distance priors, with and without three alternative supernova compilations, we find a nominal $2.6$--$3.6σ$ preference for nonzero relaxation over constant $w$. The composition framework also motivates a constitutive prescription for linear perturbations that remains regular at phantom crossing. Near equilibrium, regular long-wavelength composition disturbances relax at the background rate to leading order, while small-scale fluctuations propagate as damped sound waves. We prove, however, that for separately conserved matter and dark energy, the pointwise constitutive relation cannot sustain a regular, gradient-stable negative-pressure branch throughout its full past evolution. We explore modifications of the pressure response and their consistency with neighbouring homogeneous histories, identifying requirements for extending the near-equilibrium description to the full cosmological evolution.

papers.title_en: The PSR J0435+3233 Triple System
papers.abstract_en: The detailed evolution of triple star systems is complicated and poorly known. Using archived optical/infrared and $γ$-ray data, we identified the pulsar PSR~J0435+3233 as a $γ$-ray pulsar in a hierarchical triple system, with a helium white dwarf (WD) as a close inner binary companion and a Sun-like star as the distant tertiary. PSR~J0435+3233 and the WD companion are in a circular orbit with a period of $P_{\rm orb1} = 8.0$~days and an eccentricity of $e=0.00016$. The tertiary is a G-type subgiant with a mass of $0.98(12) M_\odot$ at a distance of $2.1(4)$ kpc from the Earth. By simultaneously fitting the observed spin-period variations of the $γ$-ray emission (over 16.7 years) and radio emission (over 4.9 years) from PSR~J0435+3233, the changes in the inner orbital parameters, the Shapiro delay, Gaia astrometry, and the outer companion mass, we determined the outer elliptical orbit for the tertiary, with a period $P_{\rm orb2} = 73.5$~yrs and an eccentricity $e_2 = 0.598$. The outer orbit is either nearly perpendicular to the inner orbit with a mutual inclination of $\sim 85^\circ$, or moderately inclined by $\sim 54^\circ$. For the former geometry, the pulsar, the WD, and the tertiary star have masses of $1.16(5) M_\odot$, $0.273(8) M_\odot$, and $0.91(5) M_\odot$, respectively; for the latter geometry, the corresponding masses are $1.34(15) M_\odot$, $0.305(23) M_\odot$, and $1.13(7) M_\odot$. This is a unique triple system for detailed multi-band observations and for studying the evolutionary path and dynamic processes of a primordial triple star system. It will ultimately evolve into a system consisting of a neutron star and two white dwarfs.

papers.title_en: Anomaly induced transport in holographic superconductors
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the anomaly-induced transport properties of a holographic superconductor exhibiting spontaneous symmetry breaking. The holographic model incorporates vector and axial gauge fields, an additional non-anomalous $U(1)$ symmetry, and a charged scalar field that drives the phase transition. Working in the probe limit, we numerically construct the superconducting background under two alternative scalar field quantizations, corresponding to operators with scaling dimensions $Δ=1$ and $Δ=3$ (denoted as the $O_1$ and $O_2$ theories, respectively). Using Kubo formulae, we compute the chiral magnetic conductivities and examine their response to the scalar condensate. Our findings demonstrate that spontaneous symmetry breaking allows anomaly-induced transport to extend beyond anomalous currents, significantly impacting the non-anomalous sector as well. Remarkably, this effect appears in both theories, indicating that the influence on the non-anomalous sector is independent of the chosen quantization. The comparison of our numerical results with the analytical limits for $O_i \to 0$ and $O_i \to \infty$ $(i=1,2)$ reveals consistent behavior across both theories.

papers.title_en: Bogoliubov-de Gennes spectrum, Cherenkov radiation and recoil of solitons with third-order dispersion underlying optical analogue horizons
papers.abstract_en: Third-order dispersion turns the soliton of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation, which underlies optical analogues of event horizons in fibers, into a weakly radiating solitary wave. We compute three of its properties without assuming a thermal emission law. First, the linearized (Bogoliubov-de Gennes) problem must be posed about the stationary state of the dispersive equation: linearizing about the integrable profile produces a complex quartet that is converged in grid and box, grows as the square root of the dispersion strength and is spurious. About the stationary state, on a periodic grid, the zero-mode sector consists of two Jordan blocks of size two and the spectrum is real at the operating point, including negative-energy box modes of the resonant branch. Second, we measure the steady Cherenkov emission of adiabatically prepared solitons from the flux of the radiation behind them, over eight decades. The radiation is phase-matched in the frame of the drifting soliton, and the first-order rate falls short of the measured one by factors of 29 to 45. Expressed through a scaled dispersion coefficient of the local soliton, the measured rate describes launched solitons of three amplitudes; with norm and momentum balance, and no further fitted parameter, it reproduces their recoil and the slow decay of their loss rate; at weak dispersion the loss of a launched soliton is the shedding of its launch mismatch. Third, a census of the asymptotic channels shows that long-wavelength upstream emission requires the chemical potential of the soliton, lowered by the comoving-frame Doppler shift of a drifting soliton, to lie inside the analysis band, which bounds the soliton amplitude. In a kinematic model of the flow the surface gravity has a closed form; the thermal relation and the entanglement built on it are imposed inputs of that model. The construction applies to Raman-free Kerr media.

papers.title_en: Nonaxisymmetric (2+1) black holes with Dym boundary conditions
papers.abstract_en: We present the spectrum of stationary black hole solutions associated with the first nontrivial member of the Dym family of boundary conditions. The analysis combines the holonomy conditions provided by the Chern-Simons formulation of AdS$_3$ gravity with the periodic solutions of the stationary Dym equation. The resulting spacetimes are characterized by two positive real parameters, two positive integers, and a relative phase, generically describing stationary, nonaxisymmetric black holes.

papers.title_en: Liouvillian interpolation of the self-energy of cluster dynamical mean-field theories
papers.abstract_en: Two widely-used non-local extensions of dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), namely cellular DMFT (CDMFT) and the dynamical cluster approximation (DCA), both yield self-energies marred by having some unphysical properties: CDMFT yields real-space self-energies that are not translationally invariant, and DCA yields momentum-space self-energies with discontinuities in their momentum dependence. It is often desirable to remove these flaws by post-processing cluster DMFT results, using strategies called periodization for CDMFT and interpolation for DCA---for brevity, we refer to both cases as \textit{interpolation}. However, traditional interpolation approaches struggle to reliably capture intricate structures such as hole pockets in the hole-doped square-lattice Hubbard model. Further, these approaches interpolate frequency-dependent functions, which may lead to causality violations. Here, we propose \textit{Liouvillian interpolation}, a novel, intuitive, and robust scheme for interpolating cluster DMFT results. Our key idea is to interpolate frequency-\textit{independent} matrix elements of the single-particle irreducible part of the Liouvillian, obtained from a continued-fraction expansion of the cluster DMFT self-energy. We demonstrate that the ingredients of such an expansion possess a more local Fourier expansion than the functions involved in traditional interpolation schemes, and that Liouvillian interpolation conserves causality by construction. We illustrate our method for the one-dimensional Hubbard model using CDMFT, and for the two-dimensional Hubbard model using four-site CDMFT and four-patch DCA. For the latter, $\mathcal{L}$-interpolation can (depending on doping) yield Fermi and Luttinger arcs which together seem to form a closed surface.

papers.title_en: New approach to the calculation of extreme-mass-ratio inspirals with a spinning secondary
papers.abstract_en: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) are among the most promising sources for future space-based gravitational-wave (GW) detectors, such as the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna. To fully leverage the scientific potential, the GW templates required for parameter estimation must be modeled with high accuracy for eccentric precessing binary systems with nonzero spins. This work introduces a practical and efficient framework for incorporating the effects of secondary spin in fully generic, eccentric, and off-equatorial EMRIs to the first postadiabatic order. We utilize recently found analytic solutions for the trajectories of spinning bodies in Kerr spacetime to significantly simplify the calculation of the corresponding asymptotic GW fluxes. Furthermore, thanks to the recently proven flux-balance laws, we show how to express the rates of change of the constants of motion, including the Carter-Rüdiger constant, using asymptotic Teukolsky amplitudes and purely geodesic functions that are already established in the literature. Finally, we show how this framework performs in the case of nearly spherical inspirals and numerically demonstrate that the linear-in-spin part of the phases is gauge independent. A Wolfram Mathematica implementation of the code developed in this work is publicly available in the KerrSpinningFluxes package.

papers.title_en: Bessel-Hagen currents, reducibility charges, and local gravitational energy
papers.abstract_en: We consider whether the translation Noether current of a linearised metric spin-2 theory admits a strictly gauge-invariant local representative. For Fierz-Pauli and dynamically regular pure curvature-squared theories in four dimensions, we show that no such representative exists under the stated locality, polynomiality and covariance assumptions. A direct enumeration first excludes nonzero symmetric rank-two tensors at the dimension and derivative order of the quadratic action: in the curvature-squared case, the parity-even conservation kernel consists of the identically vanishing Lanczos--Lovelock combination, while both parity-odd coefficients vanish. Homogeneity of the actions in total derivative number then allows projection by field degree and derivative number, extending the exclusion to all finite-order local polynomial representatives with constant coefficients and no explicit coordinate dependence. The translation current nevertheless defines a nonzero conserved-current class. Independently, a constant translation is a Killing reducibility parameter of the linearised gauge symmetry and determines a nonzero linear surface-charge class, which is distinct from the quadratic energy current. A separate calculation shows why a direct compensator cancellation available in Maxwell theory fails for the metric spin-2 field, although this calculation is not needed for the current-class result. Maxwell theory, propagating free $p$-forms and Yang--Mills theory linearised about the trivial vacuum provide comparisons in which translations are not reducibility parameters and strictly gauge-invariant stress tensors exist. Gauss--Bonnet and pure flat-space $R^2$ gravity lie outside the regular scope of the result, through variational triviality and dynamical degeneracy, respectively.

papers.title_en: Instabilities in self-consistent diagrammatic approaches and how to cure them
papers.abstract_en: While self-consistent diagrammatic approaches are widely used to compute the physical properties of correlated quantum materials, their applicability may get severely hindered precisely in the parameter regions where the most exciting physics is observed. One of the major issues, referred to as "misleading convergence", is the tendency of iterative schemes to converge to unphysical fixed points for intermediate-to-strong electronic interactions, regardless of the numerical accuracy of the computation. Here, we explicitly verify that the origin of this problem in several established self-consistent many-electron approaches, defined in the general diagrammatic framework of the boson-exchange formalism, resides exclusively in the stability condition of the respective iteration schemes, and not in an intrinsic breakdown of their self-consistent diagrammatic description. This insight enables a simple and general remedy, as recently proposed in Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016502 (2026): The redefinition of the iterative procedure, by inverting the unstable eigendirections of the Jacobian associated with the fixed point of the self-consistent algorithm. We illustrate the successful outcome of this procedure by means of systematic calculations performed on exactly solvable testbed models. Our results demonstrate that the physical fixed point of the diagrammatic schemes we considered can be stabilized, de facto, across the entire parameter range, including the most challenging nonperturbative/strong-coupling regimes.

papers.title_en: Relativistic dynamical friction in Kerr-Schild coordinates
papers.abstract_en: Simulations of the evolution of matter on static metric backgrounds allow us to estimate backreaction effects like dynamical friction at first order in the matter density. Previous simulations of dynamical friction have used boosted isotropic and quasi-isotropic Kerr coordinates, which simplifies the extraction of the relevant diagnostics but results in a more complicated implementation of the evolution. In particular, the lack of horizon penetrating coordinates means that high resolutions are needed to ensure convergence, and the boosted, spinning black hole metric cannot easily be written in a closed form, making it more costly to evaluate. In this paper we describe how to reformulate the calculation of the diagnostics in the boosted Kerr-Schild frame for the non-spinning case. We verify that our implementation reproduces previous results quantifying dynamical friction in wave-like dark matter in the appropriate regimes. We discuss the subtleties of transforming diagnostic observables between frames in a 3+1 evolution and develop a general framework for this process.

papers.title_en: Proof of a magnificent conjecture
papers.abstract_en: Motivated by super-Yang-Mills theory on a Calabi-Yau 4-fold, Nekrasov and Piazzalunga have assigned weights to $r$-tuples of solid partitions and conjectured a formula for their weighted generating function. We define $K$-theoretic virtual invariants of Quot schemes of 0-dimensional quotients of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}^4}^{\oplus r}$ by realizing them as zero loci of isotropic sections of orthogonal bundles on non-commutative Quot schemes. Via the Oh-Thomas localization formula, we recover Nekrasov-Piazzalunga's weights and derive their sign rule. Our proof passes through refining the $K$-theoretic invariants to sheaves and describing them via Clifford modules, which lets us show that they arise from a factorizable sequence of sheaves in the sense of Okounkov. Taking limits of the equivariant parameters, we then deduce the Nekrasov-Piazzalunga conjecture from its 3-dimensional analog.

papers.title_en: Energy-Energy Correlators at Strong Coupling
papers.abstract_en: We study energy-energy correlators (EEC) in planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory at strong 't Hooft coupling $λ$. We consider the EEC in states created by half-BPS operators of arbitrary dimension $p$, and determine the corresponding event-shape function up to order $λ^{-3/2}$ from the worldsheet representation of the AdS Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude with Kaluza-Klein external states. For $p=2$ we compute the second curvature correction, which completes the EEC through order $λ^{-2}$; the new contribution improves the agreement with recently derived non-perturbative bounds at intermediate coupling. We further develop a complementary method in which the strong-coupling expansion coefficients of the EEC are extracted directly from the Wilson coefficients of low-energy expansion of the AdS Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude, and find the two approaches in perfect agreement.

papers.title_en: A discrete analogue of $\mathscr{N}=2$ super Weil-Petersson volumes
papers.abstract_en: We introduce a discrete spectral curve from $\mathscr{N}=2$ double-scaled SYK whose topological recursion defines quasi-polynomial volumes in integer boundary lengths. The curve has two edge theories: a local $\mathscr{N}=2$ theory at the lower edge and a bosonic theory at the upper edge. Focusing on the local $\mathscr{N}=2$ theory, we compute its finite-$q$ volumes and independently check the first few using the string equation. In the $q\rightarrow 1$ continuum limit, these recover the super Weil-Petersson volumes of Turiaci and Witten. Finally, we give an all-genus intersection-theoretic interpretation of these local volumes on the moduli space of stable marked curves, in terms of a deformed spin class with a gap-dependent $κ$-class dressing.

papers.title_en: A new approach to the Kondo effect: sophomore's dream function and Lee-Yang zeros
papers.abstract_en: We develop an analytical approach to the Kondo problem based on an effective partition function that generalizes the sophomore's dream integral. The Kondo crossover is represented as a passage through an approximately equidistant ladder of its Lee-Yang zeros in the complex plane, rather than as a singularity on the real axis. Summation over this ladder yields the Gamma function $Γ(α+ T_K/(2 πT))$ as the universal crossover backbone, where the offset $α=1/2$ is fixed by the Friedel sum rule. The Euler-Maclaurin expansion connects the discrete zero structure to the Nozieres Fermi-liquid theory through Bernoulli numbers. A two-cutoff formula provides a compact, essentially one-parameter description of the full crossover in terms of a temperature-space Fano lineshape which is a thermal average of the energy-space Fano resonance observed in STM. Drift corrections are treated. The approach extends to $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ Coqblin-Schrieffer, underscreened and Anderson impurity models, and Kondo lattices.

papers.title_en: Metastable cosmic strings are broken at the start
papers.abstract_en: We show that metastable cosmic strings break at early times, either via finite-temperature effects or by attaching to pre-existing monopoles during network percolation. The resulting segments can be initially super-horizon in size and thus persist for a significant amount of time. If the strings do not re-percolate, the network's eventual destruction is typically due to this early-time breaking rather than late-time quantum tunnelling. Survival of strings to epochs probed by NANOGrav requires $m_M^2/μ\gtrsim 10^3$, where $m_M$ and $μ$ are the monopole mass and the string tension respectively, over an order of magnitude larger than previous estimates. We also revisit quantum-tunnelling induced breaking. Results from numerical simulations suggest that this occurs mainly at rare high-tension points on the strings, yielding a rate much larger than is usually assumed. We briefly discuss the related scenario of flux tubes in a dark QCD-like hidden sector with dark-quark masses above the confinement scale.

papers.title_en: Scalar nonstandard neutrino interactions in galactic supernovae
papers.abstract_en: We analyze the prospects for studying scalar nonstandard interactions (SNSI) using the neutrino burst from a galactic supernova (SN). SNSI modifies the resonant flavor conversion and, correspondingly, the neutronization burst signal, and may be identifiable in future multi-tonne-scale experiments, such as Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE). Notably, in the normal mass ordering, SNSI can lead to an anomalous (re)appearance of the neutronization-burst $ν_e$ peak at Earth, a feature otherwise strongly suppressed in the Standard Model. We show that, in the presence of SNSI, neutrinos propagating out of the dense SN environment acquire a density-squared-dependent contribution to their mass-squared differences, which in turn modifies the energy levels of the neutrino matter eigenstates. This density-squared effect is absent in less dense environments such as the Earth or the Sun and is precisely what enables SN neutrinos to probe SNSI parameters up to 4 orders of magnitude below the values accessible to solar or terrestrial neutrino sources.

papers.title_en: The Gregory-Laflamme Instability of five-dimensional Black Strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet Gravity
papers.abstract_en: We complement and extend our recent study of the non-linear evolution of the Gregory-Laflamme instability of black strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity in five spacetime dimensions. First, we study time-dependent perturbations of uniform black strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet theory and determine the growth rates as a function of the coupling. We find that for positive Gauss-Bonnet couplings, the black strings are more unstable than in general relativity in the sense that the growth rates are larger and shorter wavelengths are unstable. In the second part of the paper we show that the hyperbolicity of the equation of motion of Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet theory is determined by an effective metric when the dynamics is restricted to spherical symmetry in the asymptotically flat directions. When the effective field theory becomes strongly coupled, as it happens near the endpoint of the Gregory-Laflamme instability of the black string, this effective metric becomes degenerate and the Cauchy evolution breaks down. Applying this criterion to uniform black strings, we find that for any positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling there is an open set of regular solutions (including the one of minimal thickness) on which the effective metric degenerates in a neighbourhood of the horizon. Therefore, we argue that these solutions cannot be attained from weakly coupled initial data by Cauchy evolution and the solutions of the linearized equations around them cannot be interpreted as approximations to nearby non-linear evolutions. We provide further evidence for this picture with non-linear simulations of the Gregory-Laflamme instability. The non-linear simulations terminate through a loss of hyperbolicity of the Tricomi or Keldysh type, depending on the sign of the Gauss-Bonnet coupling.

papers.title_en: Inpainting to search for premerger massive black hole binaries in realistic LISA datasets
papers.abstract_en: A key science target of the Large Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is to carry out multi-messenger observations of massive black hole binaries, observing the merger simultaneously in gravitational waves and with electromagnetic observatories. Identifying that a merger is happening and providing an updating estimate of the sky location in the hours, days and weeks before the merger is critical to enable electromagnetic observations of the merger event. In this work we demonstrate and compare two methods for premerger identification of massive black hole binaries; a zero-latency filter approach and, for the first time, an approach using an ``inpainting'' technique. We apply these methods to the LISA Data Challenge dataset 2a--Sangria-HM--and demonstrate the successful recovery of the 14 signals in the dataset that we expected to be identifiable at least half a day before merger. We show that the inpainting method can identify premerger signals even when gaps are present in the data, demonstrating the recovery of a signal even when 3 day-long data gaps are added to the 14 days preceding merger. Finally, we explore the challenge of overlapping signals, using a region of overlapping signals in the Sangria-HM dataset, all of which merge within a 10-day window, and show how removing signals that have been confidently identified from the data allows us to identify quieter signals in the same period.

papers.title_en: Why Stellar Sequences Turn Over: Fixed Points, Instability, and Equation-of-State Universality
papers.abstract_en: We reformulate the stellar structure equations in the language of dynamical systems and show that the maximum mass of stellar sequences arises from the existence of a fixed point in the relativistic regime. In an appropriate representation of the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations, this fixed point becomes manifest and is directly associated with the turnover of the mass-radius curve. The existence of a fixed point implies an effective reduction in dimensionality near the onset of instability, which provides a simple explanation for several equation-of-state-insensitive relations and predicts new ones. In the weakly relativistic limit, we identify a complementary universal structure shared by stellar sequences at their maximum mass, which we term the "compressible limit," and derive distinct universal relations governing the maximum mass in the Newtonian and post-Newtonian regimes. Combining these theoretical results with current astrophysical constraints, we show that the J0740+6620 pulsar is unlikely to lie near the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff maximum mass unless the equation of state exhibits a strong first-order phase transition at densities just above its central density.

papers.title_en: Joint Model-independent Constraints on the Post-Newtonian Parameter and Cosmic Curvature from Galaxy-scale Strong Lensing, SNe Ia, BAO, and Cosmic Chronometers
papers.abstract_en: This investigation aims to test the validity of general relativity (GR) on kiloparsec scales via galaxy-scale strong gravitational lensing (SGL) combined with multiple cosmological probes. To circumvent the circularity problem induced by the presumption of a cosmological model based on GR, we apply the distance sum rule in the Friedmann-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) metric to constrain the post-Newtonian parameter gamma PPN and spatial curvature Omega k independently of any cosmological model. The study introduces two methodological improvements: (i) parameterizing the dark-energy evolution factor with second-order Chebyshev orthogonal polynomials, which ensures uniformly high convergence across the full redshift baseline while retaining Omega k as an explicit free parameter; (ii) extending the original two-probe configuration (SGL + Type Ia supernovae) to a four-probe joint analysis that includes baryon acoustic oscillations and cosmic chronometers. Our results show that gamma PPN = 1.119 (+0.072/-0.072) and Omega k = 0.101 (+0.077/-0.076) at 68% confidence. The gamma PPN value is consistent with the GR prediction of unity at 1.7 sigma, while Omega k favors a mildly open universe, with flatness consistent at 2 sigma. Taking model-independent constraints as a benchmark, we quantify the systematic shift in gamma PPN induced by eight representative dark energy models, and find that all offsets are negligible, well below the baseline 1 sigma uncertainty, with no significant bias at current precision. These results confirm that conventional strong-lensing gravity tests introduce no measurable systematic bias, validating our model-independent framework.

papers.title_en: G2 resolutions and backtracking in scale-separated AdS$_3$
papers.abstract_en: We study scale-separated AdS$_3$ models with full moduli stabilization in massive IIA supergravity on G2 orientifolds. In addition to constructing new examples, we investigate the properties of these models once the singularities of the G2 toroidal orbifold are resolved. The blow-up moduli are shown to be stabilized using fluxes in a parametric regime that preserves scale separation and control under the supergravity approximation. We further show that the apparent orientifold intersections in the singular orbifold description do not exist on such resolved spaces. Finally, we analyze the brane dual picture of such models using flux backtracking. We highlight several interesting features from such analysis such as a finite interval solution of the resulting flow equations in some of the models and the desirable low-energy decoupling of brane modes.

papers.title_en: Altermagnetic Control of Charge-4e Superconductivity
papers.abstract_en: We present, to our knowledge, the first theoretical realization of an independent charge-4e phase in a two-dimensional classical array of conventional superconductors coupled through altermagnetic junctions. Tuning the altermagnetic splitting suppresses the leading single-pair tunneling harmonic while retaining strong double-pair coupling, producing a finite charge-4e region between staggered and uniform charge-2e states. Using the complete temperature-dependent microscopic Josephson spectrum, we find short-range ordinary pair correlations alongside algebraic coherence of pairs of Cooper pairs. Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless scaling and a half-flux response further identify the charge-4e phase. Our results establish altermagnetism as a microscopic means to select between ordinary and composite superconducting coherence.

papers.title_en: An LSST-DESC Precursor Project: Hyper Suprime-Cam Year 1 $3\times2$pt in Harmonic Space
papers.abstract_en: We present the first fully photometric joint analysis of weak gravitational lensing and galaxy clustering (3$\times$2pt) in harmonic space with LSST-DESC analysis pipelines applied to Hyper Suprime-Cam Year 1 (HSC Y1) data. The HSC Y1 dataset, with imaging depth and galaxy number density similar to those expected for the first year of LSST observations, is an ideal testbed for validating DESC measurement and inference tools. We measure the full set of angular power spectra - cosmic shear, galaxy clustering, and galaxy-galaxy lensing - perform null tests, and correct for the impact of observing conditions on both the galaxy density and shear fields via mode deprojection. We validate our likelihood pipeline by reproducing the official HSC Y1 cosmic shear cosmological constraints with the DESC inference code. Jointly analysing all three two-point functions, we constrain $Λ$CDM and $w$CDM cosmologies, reporting results for cosmic shear, the combination of galaxy clustering and galaxy-galaxy lensing (2$\times$2pt), and the full 3$\times$2pt. From the joint 3$\times$2pt $Λ$CDM analysis we find $Ω_m = 0.249^{+0.061}_{-0.051}$, $σ_8 = 0.904^{+0.098}_{-0.091}$, and $S_8 \equiv σ_8\sqrt{Ω_m/0.3} = 0.821^{+0.018}_{-0.021}$. This analysis validates the complete DESC 3x2pt infrastructure on survey data, providing the foundation for the forthcoming LSST Year 1 cosmological analysis.
authors: the LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration

papers.title_en: Dynamical symmetry breaking in a non-polynomial four-fermion model
papers.abstract_en: We present a new four-fermion model with a strongly non-polynomial coupling. To eliminate these non-polynomialities, we introduce two auxiliary vector fields and show that the dynamical Lorentz symmetry breaking is possible in our theory, as revealed by the effective potential generated for these vector fields. We explicitly calculate the low-energy effective action for these fields, which is given by the sum of three Maxwell terms (one for each field and a mixed one) plus a potential term displaying nontrivial minima.

papers.title_en: de Sitter in String Theory vs. Gibbons & Hawking
papers.abstract_en: This paper corroborates a statement that perturbative string theory does not admit a solution whose spacetime metric is de Sitter times a closed manifold, to all orders in the $α'$ and $g_s$ expansions, under the assumption that the logarithm of the sphere partition function of Euclidean quantum gravity receives a nonzero contribution proportional to $\frac{1}{G_N}$ in a saddle-point approximation. This assumption is related to the Gibbons-Hawking proposal that the entropy of the cosmological horizon of the static patch is $\frac{A}{4G_N}$. Evidence for the statement comes from independent approaches to the effective action of string theory, all of which agree that the tree-level action vanishes for closed Euclidean target-space solutions. One possible implication is that the state of the Universe will depart from an asymptotically de Sitter spacetime.

papers.title_en: Robustness of exact $SU(N)$ Einstein-Skyrme solutions: black holes, wormholes and cosmologies
papers.abstract_en: The $SU(2)$ Skyrme model admits exact solutions when coupled to General Relativity in four spacetime dimensions. Here, we demonstrate that relevant gravitational configurations, such as black holes, wormholes, and cosmologies, are robust under the extension to $SU(N)$ with an arbitrary number of flavors. We show that key physical features, such as the thermodynamic properties, the baryon number of the configurations, and the geometry, are crucially determined by the number of flavors as well as the coupling constants of the theory. In particular: first, we prove that an increase in the matter content favors the local thermal stability of spherically symmetric black holes. Second, for cosmological solutions, we demonstrate analytically that as the hadronic matter content increases, the scale factor grows more slowly due to enhanced gravitational attraction, while the expansion rate (measured by the Hubble parameter) increases as a consequence of the higher energy density. Third, we find that the throat of traversable wormhole solutions can be enlarged by increasing the number of flavors, since the energy density required to keep the throat open does not grow indefinitely but rather saturates at a finite value.

papers.title_en: On the Utility of Textbooks in Understanding the Renaissance of General Relativity
papers.abstract_en: This paper argues for the historical utility of general relativity textbooks written during, or shortly before, the Renaissance of general relativity. More so than research papers, textbooks offer a narrative account of the field--one that may differ substantially from the accounts of other authors addressing the same subject. Textbooks on general relativity therefore constitute a distinctive form of testimony to the intellectual forces that shaped general relativity, particularly during its reinvention period from 1955 to the mid-1970s. A second pillar of this argument is the observation that nearly all principal investigators at the research centers previously identified by Lalli et al.--centers that functioned as intellectual epicenters of the Renaissance of general relativity--eventually produced a textbook associated with their own school of thought. To situate this observation within the broader development of the field, the paper presents a concise history of general relativity textbooks from the theory's inception in 1915-16 to the 1980s. This history illustrates one way in which textbooks can serve as sources for reconstructing the intellectual dynamics of the Renaissance of general relativity.

papers.title_en: Optical Depths from the Thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich Effect with ACT DR6 and DESI DR1 Spectroscopic Galaxies and Optically-Selected Clusters
papers.abstract_en: We present stacked thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ) effect measurements for three samples of galaxy groups and clusters: those traced by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Data Release 1 (DESI DR1) luminous red galaxies (LRG) and the DESI DR1 Bright Galaxy Sample (BGS), and an eROMaPPer optically-selected sample from the DESI Legacy Imaging Survey. We use the latest Atacama Cosmology Telescope DR6 (ACT)+Planck component-separated internal linear combination (ILC) Compton-$y$ maps and ACT+Planck coadded 90, 150, and 220 GHz temperature maps to extract the tSZ signal within a $\sim2'$ disk aperture for sources binned by luminosity, richness, or mass. We measure the average tSZ signal with high statistical significance, with signal-to-noise ratios surpassing 38 for LRG, 27 for BGS, and 39 for the eROMaPPer sample using the 90 GHz ACT DR6+Planck map. We conduct a detailed study of systematics and foregrounds such as dust and cosmic infrared background (CIB) contamination, which remain a core challenge for tSZ analysis. For the LRG and BGS samples, we find that dust and radio source emission dominate the tSZ signal at scales near and below the disk aperture radius. Large-scale ($R>4'$) contamination from the CIB is less significant. We mitigate these contaminants to isolate the tSZ signal and use a combination of simulated and real measurements to develop Compton-$y-$optical depth ($\bar y-\bar τ$) scaling relations to infer optical depths, which are found to be in agreement with values measured using the pairwise kinematic SZ effect for the same tracer samples. The $\bar y-\bar τ$ scaling relation for the eROMaPPer sample is the first such relationship to be derived directly from SZ measurements.

papers.title_en: Holographic Krylov complexity in confining backgrounds: particle, string, and frames
papers.abstract_en: We investigate holographic Krylov complexity in bottom-up holographic QCD models describing the confined phase, using the recently proposed correspondence between the growth rate of Krylov complexity and the proper radial momentum of probes, such as particles and strings, falling in the bulk spacetime. As representative confining backgrounds, we consider two horizonless geometries, namely the dilaton-deformed AdS-soliton and the deformed thermal-AdS spacetime, both arising as solutions of an Einstein-dilaton gravity system. We find that the Krylov complexity associated with a massive particle exhibits qualitatively distinct behavior in these two backgrounds when analyzed in the Einstein frame. In the deformed AdS-soliton geometry, the complexity undergoes periodic oscillations, with both the oscillation period and amplitude depending on the parameters of the model. In contrast, in the deformed thermal-AdS geometry, the complexity grows exponentially at late times and does not display oscillatory behavior. We then investigate string dynamics in the string frame and find that the Krylov complexity exhibits oscillatory behavior in both confining backgrounds. This behavior is traced to the emergence of an additional turning point in the deep infrared of the string-frame geometry. Motivated by this observation, we further analyze massive-particle dynamics in the string frame, where we find qualitatively similar behavior in the two confining backgrounds. Our results demonstrate that the Krylov complexity of confined holographic systems depends sensitively on the choice of probe and frame, while also revealing a closer correspondence between the two confining geometries in the string-frame description.

papers.title_en: Mass Proxy Quality of Halo Properties in IllustrisTNG and FLAMINGO Simulations: II. Galaxies, Stars, and Black Holes
papers.abstract_en: We study the stellar, black hole, and satellite galaxy populations of group- and cluster-scale halos in the IllustrisTNG, TNG-Cluster, and FLAMINGO cosmological hydrodynamical simulations.
